explain.say: Homesick in London, a young Irish poet heard a little fountain in a shop window and dreamed of a tiny lake island at home called Innisfree. That poet, W. B. Yeats, lived from 1865 to 1939 and changed his style more than almost any poet. The timeline follows him from Celtic dreams to hard modern verse.

explain.say: Here is the world that shaped him: Maud Gonne, a fiery nationalist he loved for decades, who refused his proposals; Lady Gregory, his patron, with whom he founded Dublin's Abbey Theatre; and Irish myth, full of heroes like Cuchulain. Yeats helped lead the Irish Literary Revival. Why does a new nation need its own stories?

At Easter 1916 rebels seized central Dublin for six days, and the British executed the leaders. Yeats had thought some of them ordinary, even foolish, but in his poem Easter, 1916 he names them and says all is changed utterly: a terrible beauty is born. Why put beauty and terror together?

explain.say: Now The Second Coming, written in 1919. Look at the reasons on the board: a world war just ended, revolution in Russia and Ireland, and Yeats's private theory of the gyres, great spinning cycles of history about two thousand years long. Things fall apart; the centre cannot hold. Why do people still quote it in every crisis?

explain.say: In old age Yeats wrote Sailing to Byzantium, an imagined voyage away from a country of the young to the ancient city of art, now Istanbul, where he longs to become a golden bird beyond time. Chinua Achebe took the title Things Fall Apart from Yeats. Superb. Challenge: compare Innisfree and Byzantium, two escapes almost forty years apart.

faq.q: What does Things fall apart; the centre cannot hold mean?
faq.a: In The Second Coming, Yeats pictures order collapsing after the First World War and revolutions, as society loses its centre and violence spreads. He saw it as the end of a two-thousand-year cycle of history.
The refrain of Easter, 1916: the Rising and the executions transformed ordinary people into martyrs. It is beautiful because heroic and terrible because it means death and hardened hearts.
asks: A terrible beauty is born meaning

faq.a: Interlocking spinning cones from Yeats's mystical book A Vision, standing for opposing forces in history and the soul. He believed each historical era lasts about two thousand years before reversing.

An English-born Irish nationalist and actress whom Yeats loved from 1889. She refused his proposals and married John MacBride, who was executed after the 1916 Rising. She appears in many of his poems.

faq.q: What is Sailing to Byzantium about?
faq.a: An ageing speaker leaves a country devoted to youth and sensual life for Byzantium, a symbol of timeless art, asking to be gathered into the artifice of eternity as a golden mechanical bird.

facts: Yeats won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1923.
The Abbey Theatre, co-founded by Yeats and Lady Gregory, opened in Dublin in December 1904.
The Second Coming was written in January 1919 and first published in 1920.
